item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will embark on official visit to Canada and USA from 25th August to 2nd September 2026
Union Finance Minister Smt. Sitharaman and Canadian Minister of Finance and National Revenue H.E. Mr. François-Philippe Champagne to participate in inaugural Economic and Financial Dialogue between the two countries
FM Smt. Sitharaman will participate in Roundtable discussions with leading investors, businesses and financial sector representatives, besides one-on-one high-level interaction with private sector during the visit to Canada and USA
Union Finance Minister will lead the Indian delegation at G20 FMCBG meeting under the US G20 Presidency
Union Finance Minister will also interact with Indian communities based in Toronto and Chicago to strengthen people-to-people and economic linkages
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 3:40PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will later undertake an official visit to Canada and the United States of America from 25th August to 2nd September 2026, with a focus on strengthening bilateral economic and financial partnerships, deepening investment linkages and advancing cooperation on shared global economic priorities.

During her visit to Toronto, Canada, Smt. Sitharaman will participate in the inaugural Economic and Financial Dialogue with H.E. Mr. François-Philippe Champagne, Minister of Finance and National Revenue of Canada. The Dialogue will provide an important platform for both sides to exchange views on macroeconomic developments, financial sector cooperation, bilateral investment opportunities and shared international priorities, and to further strengthen the economic and financial pillar of the renewed India-Canada partnership.

Bilateral discussions in recent months have also focused on opportunities in areas including energy, critical minerals, technology, innovation and resilient supply chains, alongside ongoing efforts towards a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).

Smt. Sitharaman will participate in an Investment Roundtable with leading CEOs, Presidents and senior representatives, chief among them are from the energy, artificial intelligence and critical minerals sectors. The interaction will seek to facilitate greater business-to-business linkages, identify investment opportunities and promote long-term commercial partnerships between India and Canada, including opportunities in GIFT City-IFSC.

In another Business Roundtable, the Union Finance Minister will engage with senior business leaders on opportunities for Canada-India cooperation, long-term investment and growth of the financial sector. Senior Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officers of Indian Public Sector Banks will also participate in the discussions, providing an opportunity to explore avenues for greater financial-sector collaboration and investment linkages.

The Canadian Club of Toronto, in partnership with the Canada-India Business Council, will host a fireside conversation between Smt. Sitharaman and H.E. Mr. Champagne on advancing shared economic interests between the two countries. The discussion will cover the renewed Canada-India bilateral relationship, the investment climate, domestic economic priorities and the evolution and future trajectory of India-Canada economic and financial relations.

Smt. Sitharaman will also hold one-to-one meetings with CEOs and senior leadership of companies based in Canada, with discussions expected to focus on investment opportunities, India's growth prospects and avenues for expanding the presence of Canadian businesses in India.

The Union Finance Minister will also participate in an interaction with the Indian diaspora in Toronto, providing an opportunity to engage with the Indian community and acknowledge its important role in strengthening people-to-people and economic linkages between India and Canada.

During the United States leg of the visit, Smt. Sitharaman will travel to Chicago, Asheville and New York from 28th August to 2nd September 2026.

In Chicago, Smt. Sitharaman will participate in an Roundtable Conference with prominent investors and engage with leading CEOs, Presidents and senior representatives of the private sector. Bilateral one-to-one meetings with CEOs and senior leadership of select companies in Chicago will also be held. The discussions will focus on India's investment opportunities, economic outlook and areas for strengthening business and investment partnerships between India and the United States.

Smt. Sitharaman will also visit the Polsky Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation at the University of Chicago, where she will exchange perspectives on entrepreneurship, innovation, technology commercialisation and strengthening linkages with India's rapidly expanding startup and innovation ecosystem.

The Union Finance Minister will also interact with members of the Indian community in Chicago during her visit.

In Asheville, North Carolina, Smt. Sitharaman will lead the Indian delegation at the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG) Meeting under the United States Presidency of the G20. The meeting, scheduled for 31st August and 1st September, will bring together Finance Ministers, Central Bank Governors and senior economic officials from G20 members to deliberate on key global economic and financial issues. The meeting follows the G20 Finance and Central Bank Deputies Meeting scheduled for 29th and 30th August.

India's participation in the G20 Finance Track provides an important platform to contribute to discussions on global economic growth and stability, international financial cooperation and other issues of significance to emerging and advanced economies. The engagement will also provide an opportunity for India to advance its perspectives on contemporary global economic challenges and strengthen cooperation with G20 partners.

In New York, Smt. Sitharaman will participate in an Investor Roundtable with CEOs and senior representatives of leading New York-based companies. She will also hold one-to-one meetings with senior executives and CEOs from the financial sector to discuss investment opportunities, India's economic and financial landscape, and avenues for strengthening financial and institutional linkages between India and the United States.

During her visit to New York, NASDAQ — a pioneering global electronic marketplace and one of the world's leading technology-driven financial market platforms — will host Smt. Sitharaman in the bell-ringing ceremony. The visit will provide an opportunity to gain insights into developments in technology-driven financial markets and the evolving interface between technology and capital markets.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
item.description: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change India restored 21.76 mn ha Land during 2011–2020, generating 1.22 bn person-days of Employment: Shri Bhupender Yadav at UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia Land Restoration is India's established National Priority, integral to Sustainable Land Management, Biodiversity Conservation, Climate Action and Rural Development: Union Environment Minister Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 2:58PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today said that land restoration is an established…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India restored 21.76 mn ha Land during 2011–2020, generating 1.22 bn person-days of Employment: Shri Bhupender Yadav at UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
Land Restoration is India's established National Priority, integral to Sustainable Land Management, Biodiversity Conservation, Climate Action and Rural Development: Union Environment Minister
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 2:58PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today said that land restoration is an established national priority for India and is integral to the country’s efforts on sustainable land management, biodiversity conservation, climate action and rural development. Speaking at a side event organised by the IUCN at the 17th Conference of the Parties (CoP 17) to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, Shri Yadav said India views restoration not as a standalone intervention, but as an essential component of sustainable and resilient development.

The Minister said India is among the major global pledgers to the Bonn Challenge. In 2015, India made an initial commitment to restore degraded and deforested land, which was subsequently enhanced to 26 million hectares by 2030. He said this commitment reflects both the scale of the challenge and India’s confidence in its national capacity to deliver restoration at scale.

Shri Yadav said India has recently released its Second Progress Report on the Bonn Challenge, covering the period 2011–2020. During this period, 21.76 million hectares were brought under restoration, supported by significant convergent financial flows and generating approximately 1.22 billion person-days of employment, he said. The Minister said these figures demonstrate that restoration can deliver both environmental and socio-economic outcomes by reviving degraded landscapes while creating employment and supporting rural livelihoods. Importantly, he said, the assessment goes beyond measuring hectares. It captures restoration across forests, agriculture, soil and water conservation and other land-use systems, recognising that restoration must respond to the ecological and socio-economic characteristics of each landscape.

The reporting process has also highlighted the need to further strengthen systems for monitoring restoration outcomes, financial flows and livelihood impacts, Shri Yadav said. India is therefore undertaking the next reporting cycle for 2021–2025, in collaboration with the ICFRE Centre of Excellence on Sustainable Land Management and IUCN. This cycle will focus on three key dimensions – area restored, financial flows and employment generated – while strengthening the national evidence base for restoration. The Minister said the credibility of any commitment ultimately rests on implementation. India has therefore developed a multi-sectoral and landscape-based approach to translating this ambition into action.

The Green India Mission, Shri Yadav informed, is strengthening forest and tree cover, ecosystem services and climate resilience. Through the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority, substantial resources are being directed towards compensatory afforestation and allied restoration activities. The Nagar Van Yojana for urban greening extends the restoration agenda to urban and peri-urban landscapes through urban forestry and green spaces. These efforts are complemented by watershed development, agroforestry, soil and water conservation and community-based restoration across the country, the Minister said.

Shri Yadav stated that this experience demonstrates that restoration cannot be delivered through a single programme or sector. It requires convergence across landscapes, sectors and levels of governance – from local communities and States to the Union Government. Looking beyond 2030, the Minister said India’s objective must be not only to restore more land, but to restore better, finance better and deliver measurable and lasting outcomes.The Minister  said this will require innovative financing mechanisms to mobilise greater public and private investment; stronger regional and international partnerships to share knowledge, technologies and experience; and sustained participation of local communities. Restoration is ultimately sustained by the people who depend upon and manage these landscapes, the Minister added.

Shri Yadav concluded by stating that India remains committed to working with international partners to advance restoration at scale. India’s experience demonstrates that ambitious commitments can be translated into measurable outcomes when supported by strong institutions, sustained financing, sound science, robust monitoring and partnerships across sectors and levels of governance. He said India looks forward to working with all partners in advancing this shared agenda.

item.description: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Proposes Amendments to Medical Devices Rules, 2017 to Promote Ease of Doing Business Proposed amendments seek to simplify regulatory requirements, standardize testing fees and facilitate faster market access for eligible medical devices Loan Licensing requirements removed for outsourced sterilization activities Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 2:21PM by PIB Delhi The Government has introduced key regulatory reforms in the medical device sector with a view to promoting Ease of Doing Business…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Proposes Amendments to Medical Devices Rules, 2017 to Promote Ease of Doing Business
Proposed amendments seek to simplify regulatory requirements, standardize testing fees and facilitate faster market access for eligible medical devices
Loan Licensing requirements removed for outsourced sterilization activities
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 2:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has introduced key regulatory reforms in the medical device sector with a view to promoting Ease of Doing Business (EoDB), simplifying regulatory processes, enhancing transparency and facilitating timely access to advanced medical technologies in the country.

Towards this objective, the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 have recently been amended to simplify the regulatory framework governing outsourced sterilization of medical devices and to expand the list of recognized stringent regulatory jurisdictions for waiver of clinical investigation requirements.

The amendment to Rule 44 of the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 has been finalized after extensive stakeholder consultations with the objective of simplifying regulatory compliance for medical device manufacturers availing outsourced sterilization facilities.

Under the amended provisions, manufacturers outsourcing product sterilization to another facility holding a valid licence under the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 will no longer be required to obtain a separate loan licence for the outsourced sterilization activity.

The amendment eliminates the requirement for a separate loan licensing process in such cases, thereby reducing duplication, administrative burden, compliance costs and associated timelines, particularly for manufacturers that do not have in-house sterilization facilities.

The amended provision also provides a six-month transition period for implementation of the new labelling requirement. This will allow manufacturers adequate time to make necessary changes to their labelling, packaging and related processes before the provision comes into effect.

The reform seeks to strike a balance between regulatory oversight and ease of doing business by simplifying the licensing framework while retaining an essential traceability mechanism for outsourced sterilization.

The measure is expected to provide greater operational flexibility to manufacturers, facilitate faster and more efficient manufacturing processes, and support the growth and competitiveness of India’s medical device industry.

Additionally, Rule 63 of the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 has been amended to include the European Union (EU) among the recognized stringent regulatory jurisdictions for waiver of clinical investigation requirements for medical devices without predicate devices.

The provision currently recognizes the United States of America, United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Japan. With the inclusion of the European Union, eligible medical devices that have already been approved in the EU will be able to benefit from the waiver provisions, facilitating faster patient access to advanced medical technologies in India.

The amendment is also expected to reduce the regulatory burden and associated timelines for importers and manufacturers while strengthening international regulatory convergence in the medical device sector.

These reforms are expected to simplify regulatory processes, reduce costs, enhance transparency and predictability, and facilitate the timely availability of advanced and innovative medical devices in India.

The measures represent an important step towards strengthening the medical device regulatory ecosystem and promoting greater Ease of Doing Business, while continuing to maintain robust standards of quality, safety and performance of medical devices.

The Official Gazette notification may be accessed through this link: https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2026/275637.pdf

*****

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President launches India’s first non-GMO high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed in Andhra Pradesh
Vice-President calls for technology, innovation and self-reliance to transform Indian agriculture
Indigenous popcorn maize hybrid reflects Aatmanirbhar Bharat in its fullest form: Vice-President
“A small beginning should lead to a big vision and a big dream”: Vice-President hails Gourmet Popcornica’s journey from Andhra Pradesh to global markets
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 2:05PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today launched India’s first non-GMO, high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed at Musunuru in Eluru district of Andhra Pradesh, describing it as a significant step towards Aatmanirbhar Bharat in agriculture. He also felicitated best-performing farmers from Andhra Pradesh and seven other States and partners associated with Gourmet Popcornica.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today launched India’s first non-GMO, high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed, developed by Gourmet Popcornica, at Musunuru in Andhra Pradesh, calling it a significant step towards Aatmanirbhar Bharat in agriculture.

He highlighted the… pic.twitter.com/3J3lX01ejX

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 24, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said farmers are the backbone of the nation and agriculture has shaped India’s civilisational and cultural life. He emphasised the importance of technology, innovation and indigenous seed development in strengthening Indian agriculture.

Referring to the launch, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said India had for years depended on imported hybrid technology for high-quality popcorn maize. The new indigenous hybrid, he said, marks an important step towards reducing such dependence and conserving foreign exchange. He commended Gourmet Popcornica and farmers for developing an Indian solution, grown on Indian soil, with the potential to compete in global markets.

The Vice-President appreciated Union Government’s farmer-centric initiatives, including PM-KISAN, PM Fasal Bima Yojana, National Food Security and Nutrition Mission and Namo Drone Didi. He also commended Chief Minister Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu for his visionary initiatives in agriculture and rural development, including Rythu Bazaars, promotion of horticulture and natural farming, and farmer-centric support systems.

Highlighting the scale of the farmer-enterprise partnership, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that more than 17,500 farmers across eight States, cultivating nearly 40,000 acres, are part of the Gourmet Popcornica journey. He lauded the journey of Shri S.B.P. Pattabhi Rama Rao and Gourmet Popcornica from a homegrown enterprise in Andhra Pradesh to a major popcorn maize processing enterprise, strengthening market access and income opportunities for thousands of farming families.

The Vice-President said a developed India will be built “from the ground”- from the soil cultivated by farmers, the seeds perfected by scientists and entrepreneurs, and the self-reliance strengthened acre by acre. He said the Musunuru initiative demonstrates how innovation, entrepreneurship and farmer partnerships can create a stronger, more self-reliant and globally competitive agricultural sector.

Upon his arrival, the Vice-President also visited the Gourmet Popcornica factory and cold storage facility, where he was briefed on maize processing, quality control, packaging and storage.

The programme was attended by Governor of Andhra Pradesh Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Chief Minister Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu, Ministers of the Government of Andhra Pradesh Shri Nara Lokesh, Shri Kinjarapu Atchannaidu and Shri Kolusu Parthasarathy, along with other dignitaries and representatives of Gourmet Popcornica.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
AIIA Launches “GARBHINI MITRA” Course to Strengthen Ayurveda-Based Maternal Wellness Support
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 2:03PM by PIB Delhi

The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, an autonomous premier institution under the Ministry of Ayush, has introduced the Garbhini Mitra Course for the 2026–2027 academic session. The initiative is a structured healthcare skill-development programme aimed at creating trained personnel to provide appropriate health education, lifestyle guidance, and community-level support to women during pregnancy and the postnatal period.

The course is rooted in the traditional Ayurvedic concepts of Garbhini Paricharya (antenatal care), Sutika Paricharya (postnatal care), and Garbhadhana Vidhi (pre-conceptional care). Designed as a six-month offline training programme running from Monday to Friday between 3:00 PM and 5:00 PM, it equips participants with practical skills in trimester-specific dietetics, lifestyle modifications, pregnancy-safe yoga, emotional support during labour, newborn massage, and basic life support protocols. The curriculum also emphasizes infection control, sanitization, biomedical waste management, and workplace safety.

Offered at the AIIA campus in Sarita Vihar, New Delhi, the course admits 20 students per batch. Candidates who have passed the Senior Secondary (10+2) examination from any recognized board in India and are at least 18 years of age are eligible to apply. Candidates currently awaiting their 12th-grade results may also submit provisional applications.

After completing the course, candidates can pursue roles as Garbhini Mitra Assistants, Prenatal/Postnatal Care Assistants, Antenatal Wellness Guides and Maternal Health Support Workers, with opportunities in Ayush centres, maternity clinics, NGOs, community health projects and wellness institutions.

The Garbhini Mitra initiative complements, rather than replaces, clinical antenatal care. Routine check-ups, diagnostic tests, and monitoring of blood pressure and haemoglobin remain essential. Trained Garbhini Mitras support pregnant women by identifying warning signs and facilitating timely referral to qualified doctors and healthcare facilities.

The last date for submitting applications is August 31, 2026. Refer to the brochure for more details: Academic Brochure- Garbhini Mitra.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
UPI Completes 10 Years of Digital Payments Revolution- Globally Recognised as World’s Largest Real‑Time Payment System
Almost 13,000-fold Surge in Transaction Volume, Annual Transaction Volume Expands from 1.78 crore transactions in FY 2016-17 to over 24,162 crore transactions in FY 2025-26
Transaction Value Rises from ₹0.07 lakh crore in FY 2016-17 to around ₹314 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, showing an almost 4,000‑fold Increase
UPI Presently Operational in 11 Countries, Emerges as a Global Platform for Cross-Border Digital Payments
Number of Banks Live on UPI Increase From 44 in FY 2016-17 to 703 in FY 2025-26, Enabling UPI's Deep Geographic Reach and Financial Inclusion
UPI’s Success Underscores India’s Leadership in Building Scalable, Inclusive, and Innovative Digital Public Infrastructure
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 1:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Unified Payments Interface (UPI), launched on 25th August 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) under the regulatory oversight of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) completes 10 years of transforming digital payments in India. UPI has emerged as the backbone of India’s digital payments ecosystem and a critical driver of financial inclusion.

Over a decade of operations, UPI has demonstrated extraordinary scale and momentum. Annual transaction volume expanded from just 1.78 crore transactions in FY 2016-17 to over 24,162 crore transactions in FY 2025-26, representing an almost 13,000‑fold surge in transaction volume. Parallelly, transaction value rose sharply from ₹0.07 lakh crore in FY 2016-17 to approximately ₹314 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, translating into a more than 4,000‑fold increase in transaction value.

UPI has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), providing an interoperable, real-time payments platform that enables seamless peer-to-peer and peer-to-merchant transactions through a single application. Today, it is the preferred mode of payment for millions of users, transforming the way India transacts. By bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation.

This simultaneous expansion in both volume and value highlights UPI’s deepening role in supporting high‑frequency retail payments. The unprecedented scale, reliability, and interoperability achieved by UPI have received global recognition, with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) acknowledging it as the world’s largest real‑time payment system by transaction volume, underscoring India’s leadership in building scalable, inclusive, and innovative digital public infrastructure.

 

I.  The Decade in Numbers

UPI AT A GLANCE: KEY STATISTICS (NPCI)

Annual Transaction Volume (FY 2016-17 to FY 2026-27*)

Fig 1: UPI Annual Transaction Volume in Crore               *Till 31st July 2026

 

 

Annual Transaction Value (FY 2016-17 to FY 2026-27*)

 

Fig 2: UPI Annual Transaction Value in ₹ Lakh Crore                   *Till 31st July 2026

 

II.  Monthly Performance, 2026

The Year 2026 marked a significant milestone in the growth trajectory of UPI. Monthly transaction volumes crossed 2,300 crore transactions for the first time in May 2026, reaching 2,320 crore transactions, signalling a new scale of adoption. This momentum continued through the year, with July 2026 recording 2,366 crore transactions, the highest monthly transaction volume in UPI’s decade‑long journey.

 

III.  Ecosystem Strength, Banks, Apps & Geography

Banks Live on UPI, Unprecedented Participation

UPI has witnessed a steady and broad‑based expansion in institutional participation since its launch. The number of banks live on UPI increased from 44 banks in FY 2016-17, the first year of operations, to 703 banks by FY 2025-26. This onboarding covers public sector banks, private banks, small finance banks, payment banks, and cooperative banks, enabling UPI's deep geographic reach. Each bank functions as a Remitter PSP (processing outgoing transactions) and/or a Beneficiary PSP (receiving funds), with NPCI monitoring performance metrics for all participants.

Fig 4: Number of Banks Live on UPI (FY2017–2026)

 

 

 

IV.  Transaction Segmentation, P2P & P2M Analysis

An analysis of UPI transactions highlights a clear divergence between volume and value across payment types. Person‑to‑merchant (P2M) transactions account for 63% of total transaction volume, reflecting UPI’s extensive use for high‑frequency, low‑value retail payments. In contrast, person‑to‑person (P2P) transactions dominate transaction value, contributing 71%, indicating their use for higher‑ticket transfers between individuals. This contrast underscores UPI’s dual role as a mass retail payments platform and a trusted channel for larger‑value fund transfers.

 

Fig 5: UPI P2P vs P2M Split - Volume & Value

 

 

 

Transaction Distribution by Ticket Size, Micro-Payments Dominate

In FY2026, UPI transactions totalling 24,162 crore reflected the platform’s deep integration into everyday digital payment usage across the country. with particularly robust momentum in the merchant segment. P2M transactions were largely driven by small‑ticket payments, with 86% below ₹500, highlighting UPI’s deep integration into routine retail and day‑to‑day commerce, even as higher‑value transactions continued to expand. P2P transactions also showed widespread usage for low‑value transfers (59% below ₹500), while a significant 41% of transactions above ₹500 reflects UPI’s growing versatility in facilitating both regular personal payments and higher‑value fund transfers.

 

 

Fig 6: UPI transaction distribution by ticket size

 

V.  UPI on the World Stage

What began as a domestic payments innovation has today evolved into a global benchmark in digital payments.

As of 2025, UPI accounts for nearly 49 % percent of the world’s real-time payment transaction volume, a milestone recognized by the IMF.

With over 66 crores transactions processed daily, UPI has surpassed global payment network, reinforcing India’s position as the world leader in instant, secure, and inclusive digital payments.  

UPI has also emerged as a global platform for cross-border digital payments and is currently operational in 11 countries, namely United Arab Emirates, France, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, Mauritius, Qatar, Cambodia, Greece and Maldives.

 

VI.  The Road Ahead, UPI's Next Decade

The next decade of UPI is poised to drive even greater transformation in India’s digital payments landscape.  By bringing new users and merchants to the UPI Ecosystem, Government of India remains committed to enabling the next phase of UPI-led innovation and strengthening India’s digital payments ecosystem through continued policy support, technological advancement, and greater financial inclusion.

Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
Prize Distribution Function of the 58th Youth Parliament Competition, 2025-26 for schools under the Directorate of Education, Government of NCT of Delhi, and the Department of Education, NDMC
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 12:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Prize Distribution Function of the 58th Youth Parliament Competition, 2025-26 for schools under the Directorate of Education, Government of NCT of Delhi, and the Department of Education, NDMC will be held on Tuesday, the 25th of August, 2026 at the GMC Balayogi Auditorium, Parliament Library Building, Parliament House Complex, New Delhi.

Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Law and Justice; and Minister of State in the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs will preside over the function and distribute the prizes to the prize-winning students and Schools for their meritorious performance in the Competition. On this occasion, the students of “Bal Bharti Public School, Parwana Road, Pitampura, Delhi” which stood first in the 58th Youth Parliament Competition, 2025-26 for schools under the Directorate of Education, Government of NCT of Delhi, and the Department of Education, NDMC, will stage a repeat performance of their “Youth Parliament Sitting” during the Prize Distribution Function.

The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs has been organising Youth Parliament Competitions for schools in the National Capital Territory of Delhi for the past 60 years. Under the programme of Youth Parliament Competition for schools under the Directorate of Education, Government of NCT of Delhi and the Department of Education NDMC, the 58th Competition in the series was organized during 2025-26 in the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

The Youth Parliament Scheme aims at inculcating among the young generations the spirit of self-discipline, tolerance of diverse opinions, righteous expression of views, and other virtues of a democratic way of life. Besides, the scheme also acquaints the students with the practices and procedures of Parliament, techniques of discussion and debate and develops in their self-confidence, quality of leadership, and the art and skill of effective oratory.

GV Mavalankar Running Parliamentary Shield and Trophy for standing first in the Competition will be awarded to “Bal Bharti Public School, Parwana Road, Pitampura, Delhi”. The Trophy for standing first amongst New Entrant Schools will also be awarded to “Bal Bharti Public School, Parwana Road, Pitampura, Delhi”. item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Minister of State for Commerce and Industry and Electronics & Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada on Official Visit to Morocco
India–Morocco Trade, Investment and Economic Cooperation in Focus During Shri Jitin Prasada’s Visit from 24–25 August 2026
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 12:37PM by PIB Delhi

Minister of State for Commerce and Industry and Electronics & Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada is on an official visit to the Kingdom of Morocco from 24 to 25 August 2026. During the visit, both sides are expected to discuss measures to further diversify the trade basket and enhance market access opportunities.

Shri Jitin Prasada will co-chair the 7th Session of the India–Morocco Joint Commission with his counterpart, H.E. Mr. Omar Hejira, Secretary of State to the Minister of Industry and Trade, in charge of Foreign Trade, Kingdom of Morocco.

The Joint Commission meeting will provide an opportunity to review the existing areas of bilateral economic and commercial cooperation and work towards further consolidating and broadening mutually beneficial engagement. Discussions are expected to cover a wide range of areas, including trade and market access, cooperation in fertilizer production and supply, investment, industrial cooperation, customs, agriculture and food safety, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, energy and mining, renewable energy, digital transformation, transport and logistics, AYUSH, tourism, education and skills.

The two sides are also expected to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on cooperation in the field of food safety between the National Office of Food Safety (ONSSA), Morocco, and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). The MoU will facilitate the exchange of information on the safety and quality of imported food products, promote cooperation in sharing information on food testing laboratories and analytical methods, and facilitate the exchange of expertise in areas of mutual interest. It will also enable technical exchanges relating to import procedures, quality control operations, sampling, testing, packaging and labelling.

A Cultural Exchange Programme between India and Morocco for the years 2026–2030 is also expected to be signed during the Joint Commission Meeting. The Programme will promote cultural exchanges and collaboration through exchanges of artists and professionals, participation in festivals and exhibitions, cooperation in heritage conservation, and strengthened linkages among museums, libraries and archival institutions.

India and Morocco share longstanding and close relations, with significant potential for further expanding bilateral trade and investment. Bilateral merchandise trade reached around USD 4 billion in 2025. India’s major exports to Morocco include refined petroleum, pharmaceuticals, vehicles, synthetic textiles, food products and spices, while Morocco’s major exports to India include phosphates and fertilizers.

As part of the visit, Shri Jitin Prasada will hold bilateral and high-level meetings with senior Moroccan leaders. He will also participate in the India–Morocco Joint Business Forum and engage with the business community to identify new opportunities for trade, investment, partnerships and joint ventures. The Minister will further interact with business leaders in Rabat during his visit.

The visit assumes added significance as India and Morocco will commemorate the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations in 2027, providing an opportunity to further deepen the longstanding partnership between the two countries.

The visit is expected to further strengthen the institutional framework for India–Morocco economic cooperation and provide fresh impetus to bilateral trade, investment, industrial partnerships and business-to-business engagement.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India calls for Diversified, Adequate, Predictable and Sustained International Finance for Land Restoration and Drought Resilience at UNCCD CoP17, at Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
Union Environment Minister highlights India’s successful Blended Green-Finance Framework for Land Restoration
Land Restoration is Not a Cost, but an Investment in Food, Water, Biodiversity, Livelihoods and Long-term Resilience: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 12:05PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today highlighted India’s innovative and diversified financing architecture for land restoration and drought resilience at the Ministerial Dialogue on ‘Innovative Financial Mechanisms for Healthy Land and Drought Resilience’, during the 17th Conference of Parties (CoP17) of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), at Ulaanbaatar (Mongolia).

Emphasising the need for sustained investment in land restoration, Shri Yadav said, “Land restoration is not a cost, but an investment in food, water, biodiversity, livelihoods and long-term resilience”. He stressed that addressing desertification, land degradation and drought at scale requires diversified, predictable and sustained sources of finance beyond public budgets, along with stronger public-private partnerships.

The Minister highlighted India’s blended green-finance framework, which enables financing for climate-change adaptation, sustainable land use, forestry and agriculture, afforestation and biodiversity conservation. He also highlighted Sovereign Green Bonds as an avenue to mobilise capital for land restoration, drought resilience, sustainable forestry and other environmental and climate priorities.

Shri Yadav highlighted India’s Green Credit Programme, which enables public and private entities to finance restoration of degraded forest land. Credits are issued after five years of restoration and upon achieving at least 40 per cent canopy density, and may be used once for compensatory afforestation, statutory plantation or CSR obligations. He also highlighted India’s compensatory conservation regime, which channels payments received for forest diversion towards compensatory afforestation and ecosystem restoration, while corporate funding is integrated by the environmental regulatory processes.

Underscoring the importance of convergence, the Minister said that bringing public and private finance together through mechanisms such as the Green Credit Programme and compensatory afforestation funds, on the same landscape and alongside citizen participation, represents a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society approach. Shri Yadav emphasised that “Finance must be continuous, verifiable and connected to local communities.” He noted that India’s experience demonstrates what committed domestic resources can achieve, but stressed that this cannot substitute for additional, adequate and predictable international finance for restoration and drought resilience.

Concluding his address, the Minister reaffirmed India’s commitment to sharing its experience, safeguards, institutional arrangements, lessons learned and areas requiring course correction. He said, “Ultimately, innovative finance should be judged not by its design or resources mobilised, but by whether it reaches the land, ecosystems and communities that need it most and delivers lasting restoration and resilience.”

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
GENESIS Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EIR) Cohort-3 Launched at GENESIS NextGen Startup Summit - Coimbatore Edition
Call for Applications for GENESIS EIR 3.0 Now Open; Aspiring Entrepreneurs and Early-Stage Innovators Invited to Apply by 3 September 2026
MeitY Startup Hub, MSH Emerging as Key National Enabler for India’s Startup and DeepTech Ecosystem
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 11:55AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), through MeitY Startup Hub (MSH), has launched GENESIS Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EIR) Cohort 3, a national-level programme to support aspiring entrepreneurs, innovators, researchers, students and early-stage startup founders in transforming innovative ideas into technology-driven ventures. GENESIS EIR 3.0 was launched at the GENESIS NextGen Startup Summit, Coimbatore Edition, held on 4 August 2026 at Rathinam Global University, Coimbatore. The Call for Applications is now live and open to the startup and innovation ecosystem.

GENESIS EIR 3.0 is a component of the GENESIS (Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups) scheme, aimed at discovering, supporting and accelerating startups, particularly in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Through its Entrepreneur-in-Residence component, the programme provides focused funding and incubation support to help innovators, students and entrepreneurs convert early-stage ideas into pilot-ready solutions. MeitY Startup Hub, established under MeitY, serves as a national platform connecting startups, incubators, accelerators, industry, investors, mentors, academia and government stakeholders, strengthening India’s DeepTech ecosystem and supporting the innovation journey from ideation and validation to commercialisation and scale.

Launch at the GENESIS NextGen Startup Summit - Coimbatore Edition

The GENESIS NextGen Startup Summit - Coimbatore Edition was organised as a collaborative platform to inspire, connect and empower aspiring entrepreneurs, startups, innovators, researchers, students, academia, industry leaders and ecosystem partners, with a focus on promoting innovation-led entrepreneurship through knowledge sharing, mentorship, networking and ecosystem collaboration.

 

Dignitaries at the launch of GENESIS EIR 3.0, GENESIS NextGen Startup Summit – Coimbatore

Following the keynote address, the official launch of GENESIS EIR 3.0 was conducted by Dr. Panneerselvam Madanagopal, Chief Executive Officer, MeitY Startup Hub, in the presence of Thiru. Pavankumar G. Giriyappanavar, IAS, District Collector, Coimbatore; Dr. Madan A. Senthil, Chancellor, Rathinam Global University, and other distinguished dignitaries. The launch reaffirmed MeitY Startup Hub’s commitment to nurturing early-stage innovators, researchers, students and entrepreneurs through structured financial assistance, mentorship, incubation support and access to a nationwide innovation ecosystem, enabling them to transform innovative ideas into validated prototypes and scalable technology-driven ventures.

Call for Applications for GENESIS EIR 3.0

Implemented by MeitY Startup Hub, GENESIS EIR Cohort-3 supports early-stage innovators developing technology-based solutions in Electronics, Information Technology (IT), Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and DeepTech. Selected applicants will receive incubation, mentorship, ecosystem access, networking opportunities and financial assistance of up to ₹10 lakh through participating GENESIS incubators.

What Selected Innovators Can Get:

•  Financial assistance of up to ₹10 lakh

•  Access to participating GENESIS incubators

•  One-on-one mentorship and expert guidance

•  Product development and MVP support

•  Incubation and business growth support

•  Support for prototyping, technology development and validation

•  Industry and startup ecosystem connections

•  Guidance towards commercialisation and startup development

Focus Areas:

Electronics and IT domain, DeepTech, Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML), Internet of Things (IoT), Semiconductor/VLSI, Cybersecurity, Blockchain, Quantum Technologies, and AR/VR, Spatial & Immersive Technologies.

Eligibility Criteria:

1.  Applicants must be Indian citizens.

2.  Applicants may be entrepreneurs, innovators, researchers, students, or founders/co-founders of early-stage startups.

3.  The proposed innovation should be in emerging technologies in the Electronics and IT domain, DeepTech, AI/ML, IoT, Semiconductor/VLSI, Cybersecurity, Blockchain, Quantum Technologies, or AR/VR, Spatial & Immersive Technologies.

4.  The innovation should be at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 1–4 (Ideation, Proof of Concept, Prototype, MVP, or early validation stage).

5.  The startup should be based in a Tier-II or Tier-III city.

6.  The startup, if incorporated, should be less than two years old as on the date of application.

7.  The startup must not have received financial assistance exceeding ₹10 lakh under any Central or State Government scheme for the same proposed idea/startup.

Important Dates and Application Details:

The application window for GENESIS EIR Cohort-3 is open from 4 August 2026 to 3 September 2026. Interested applicants may apply online at: https://mshportal.meity.gov.in/ext/form/23966/1/apply.

Official call-for-applications creative for GENESIS EIR 3.0.

GENESIS EIR Cohort-3 is designed to help bridge the gap between an idea and a viable startup. By combining financial assistance with incubation and mentorship, the program aims to enable innovators to develop, validate and advance their technologies towards market readiness. Through this initiative, MeitY Startup Hub seeks to strengthen India's technology startup ecosystem and empower innovators from across the country to build scalable and impactful ventures.

About GENESIS

Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS) is a flagship initiative of MeitY Startup Hub designed to discover, support, grow and accelerate startups across India's Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Through its Entrepreneur-in-Residence, Pilot, Investment and DeepTech funding components, GENESIS supports startups and innovators from early ideation and experimentation through to validation, investment and scale. With a total budget outlay of ₹490 crore, the scheme seeks to unlock the entrepreneurial potential of emerging regions and connect them more deeply with India’s growing innovation ecosystem.

About the GENESIS Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EIR) Component

The Entrepreneur-in-Residence component of GENESIS provides funding of up to ₹10 lakh per startup to empower innovators, students and entrepreneurs at the ideation/prototype stage, converting early ideas into pilot-ready solutions through focused funding and incubation support.

About MeitY Startup Hub (MSH)

MeitY Startup Hub, under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is a unified national platform integrating startup, incubation and innovation initiatives to strengthen India's startup and DeepTech ecosystem, spanning schemes across ideation, incubation, acceleration, funding and scale-up support.

item.title: Indian Railways Launches a Special Drive for Cleaning and Disinfection of Drinking Water Tanks and Filters
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Railways
item.description: Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Launches a Special Drive for Cleaning and Disinfection of Drinking Water Tanks and Filters Zonal Railways Advised to Undertake Comprehensive Inspection and Rectification of Drinking-Water Infrastructure; Station-Wise Deficiencies and Action Taken to be Monitored Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 11:37AM by PIB Delhi Indian Railways has launched a special cleanliness drive across the railway network focused on cleaning and disinfection of drinking-water tanks and filtration systems to ensure the continued availability of safe and clean…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Launches a Special Drive for Cleaning and Disinfection of Drinking Water Tanks and Filters
Zonal Railways Advised to Undertake Comprehensive Inspection and Rectification of Drinking-Water Infrastructure; Station-Wise Deficiencies and Action Taken to be Monitored
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 11:37AM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has launched a special cleanliness drive across the railway network focused on cleaning and disinfection of drinking-water tanks and filtration systems to ensure the continued availability of safe and clean drinking water for passengers at railway stations.

The initiative is part of a broader action plan for strengthening drinking-water quality management across Indian Railways. The action plan emphasises frequent inspection and maintenance of the entire drinking-water system, along with water-quality testing at the source as well as at the point of consumption, rather than relying solely on end-of-pipe water testing.

During the drive, Zonal Railways will undertake comprehensive inspection of water sources, treatment and filtration plants, underground and overhead tanks, PVC tanks, water booths, taps and water dispensing points. All drinking-water tanks will be drained, desludged, scrubbed and disinfected. Measures will also be taken to ensure tight covers and appropriate protection of vents and overflow points from birds, animals and algae.

The drive will also identify deficiencies requiring corrective action. Damaged tanks, pipelines and filters will be repaired or replaced, wherever required, while ensuring that there is no cross-connection between potable and non-potable water systems. All piping forming part of the drinking-water circuit will also be checked for leakages and necessary corrective measures taken to prevent water wastage.

Special attention will be given to locations where hand pumps and borewells are being used for extraction of drinking water. Zonal Railways will ensure that water from such systems remains free from contamination and is safe for potable use.

Strengthening Water Quality Management

As part of the broader action plan, the Railway Board has advised Zonal Railways to undertake comprehensive inspection of water coolers and water purification systems. Water tanks in coolers will be thoroughly cleaned, leakages in coolers, pipelines and taps will be addressed promptly, and 100 per cent hygiene around water-cooler dispensing areas will be ensured.

UV/RO purification systems for water coolers will be checked for proper functioning and provided wherever required. Scheduled maintenance, servicing, overhauling and timely replacement of filter candles and other components will be undertaken wherever due. New or replacement UV/RO systems, based on their condition and requirement, are also to be taken up in mission mode.

The prescribed measures for cleaning, purification and quality monitoring will also be applicable to Water Vending Machines to ensure that drinking water dispensed through such facilities meets the required safety and hygiene standards.

The officials will undertake physical, chemical and bacteriological testing of water samples from identified locations, including sources, post-treatment outlets, tanks, coolers, vending machines and representative taps or booths, wherever feasible. Daily residual-chlorine monitoring will also be undertaken, with immediate re-chlorination or other corrective action wherever required.

Monitoring of Infrastructure and Corrective Action

Railway Board has directed Zonal Railways to monitor and expedite works already sanctioned for replacement and construction of new overhead and underground tanks. A summary of these sanctioned works will also be prepared, and fresh sanctions, wherever required, will be processed.

Suitable filtration and purification systems for different situations, including at-source and at-tap filtration, are also being worked out to identify and prevent contamination at various stages of the drinking-water supply chain.

Zonal Railways will submit station-wise details of deficiencies identified and the corrective action taken. This mechanism will facilitate systematic monitoring of deficiencies and ensure that issues identified during the special drive are addressed in a time-bound manner.

The action plan also envisages similar measures for drinking-water infrastructure in Railway colonies and workplaces, thereby extending the focus on safe and hygienic drinking water beyond passenger areas.

Through these coordinated measures, Indian Railways is strengthening preventive inspection, infrastructure maintenance, cleaning and disinfection, water-quality testing and corrective-action mechanisms across the drinking-water supply system. The initiative aims to ensure the continued availability of safe, clean and hygienic drinking water for passengers as well as Railway personnel.

*****

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Vanshita Jaiswal

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
NA-Allocated Talabira II & III Coal Mines Mark Record Production in FY 2025-26
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 11:25AM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India’s efforts to strengthen domestic coal production and energy security are being reinforced through coal mines allocated and auctioned under the Nominated Authority (NA) framework. Talabira II & III Open Cast Coal Mine in Odisha, allocated to NLC India Ltd. on 2 May 2016 under Schedule III of the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, is among the NA-allocated mines demonstrating strong performance across production, dispatch, technology adoption, safety, environmental management, employment and community development.

Located across Sambalpur and Jharsuguda districts, the mine has emerged as a significant contributor to domestic coal availability. In FY 2025-26, Talabira II & III achieved its highest-ever annual coal production of 19.14 MT, recording a year-on-year growth of 11.28% over the previous year. The mine also recorded its highest-ever daily production of 1,26,138.07 tonnes on 21 March 2026 and highest-ever monthly production of 3.39 MT in March 2026.

The production performance has been complemented by strong coal dispatch. In FY 2025-26, the mine achieved its highest-ever annual dispatch of 17.69 MT. Of this, approximately 10.72 MT was supplied to the power sector, while 6.97 MT was supplied to the non-regulated sector. Coal from Talabira II & III supports power-generating facilities across several States, including NTPC Darlipali, NTPC Gadarwara, NTPC Khargone, NTPC Kudgi and other power plants in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal.

The mine has maintained a sustained growth trajectory since commencement of production, with cumulative coal production reaching 72.23 MT and cumulative dispatch reaching 70.89 MT up to 14 August 2026. This performance illustrates the tangible outcomes possible through the operationalisation of coal resources allocated under the Government’s coal-block allocation framework.

Technology has been a key enabler of operational efficiency at Talabira II & III. The Digital Logistics Management System (DLMS) enables end-to-end digital monitoring of coal transportation and dispatch through RFID-based vehicle verification, AI-enabled cameras and technology-enabled entry and exit gates. Following its implementation, average entry-gate processing time reduced from 1.42 minutes to 0.54 minutes per vehicle, while tare weighment time reduced from 1.34 minutes to 0.48 minutes. The mine also deploys surface miners with dust-suppression systems, GPS-based fleet management and geo-fencing, 3D Terrestrial Laser Scanning with GNSS receivers, drone-based surveying, mechanised truck loading, Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations and CCTV surveillance.

Implementation of Digital Logistics Management System (DLMS) at Talabira II & III OCP for end-to-end digital monitoring and control of coal transportation and dispatch.

The mine’s operational performance is complemented by measures aimed at responsible and environmentally sustainable mining. Plantation has been undertaken over 23.43 hectares within the mine lease, covering 64,288 plants, and 29.48 hectares outside the mine lease, covering 65,202 plants. The mine has also installed 11.68 kW of solar power capacity, including solar street lighting in nearby villages and solar lighting within mine infrastructure. Dust-control measures include wet drilling, water sprinkling, fog cannons, fixed sprinkling systems, wind barriers, truck-washing systems and mechanised road sweeping.

Safety remains a key component of the mine’s performance, with nil fatal accidents since inception. Safety measures include a Safety Management Plan, improved haul-road and traffic management, PPE compliance, strengthened blasting procedures, safety training and near-miss reporting through the ARAN Safety App. The mine has received multiple recognitions under the Annual Mines Safety Fortnight and has secured a Five-Star Rating under the Ministry of Coal’s Star Rating Evaluation consecutively from FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25.

The impact of the mine extends beyond production and energy supply. Talabira II & III supports 3,277 employment opportunities, comprising 1,277 direct and approximately 2,000 indirect employment opportunities through transportation and allied activities. Five Project Affected Persons have received skill-development training at the Skill Development Institute, Bhubaneswar, while 101 rural youth and women have been trained in sustainable livelihood initiatives through RSETI and PMKVY centres.

Community development has also formed an important part of the project’s wider impact. CSR expenditure stood at ₹5.32 crore in FY 2025-26, supporting healthcare, drinking water, education, school transportation, rural infrastructure, sports, cultural activities and solar lighting. Health and blood-donation camps benefited around 1,500 people, while drinking-water supply through tankers benefited approximately 10,000 people. During FY 2026-27 up to July 2026, a further ₹4.20 crore was spent on initiatives including drinking-water supply, healthcare support, solar lighting, school and Anganwadi infrastructure, rural roads, community facilities and water-body rejuvenation.

Mega Medical Camp organized by Talabira II & III OCP, NLC India Ltd.

From allocation in 2016 to sustained high-capacity production, the mine has demonstrated how operationalised coal resources can contribute to domestic coal production, energy security, technology-driven mining, safety, environmental stewardship, employment generation and local development.

With record production and dispatch in FY 2025-26, cumulative production of 72.23 MT, cumulative dispatch of 70.89 MT and measurable socio-economic and environmental outcomes, Talabira II & III stands as a significant example of the impact of NA-allocated coal resources in advancing India’s energy security and supporting the broader vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

****

Shuhaib T

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
CBN busts inter-state heroin syndicate in ‘Op Black Hawk’; seizes over 18.6 kg crude heroin
Three members of inter-state trafficking network arrested
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 10:03AM by PIB Delhi

In a major breakthrough against drug trafficking, officers of the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) MP and UP Units successfully executed ‘Operation Black Hawk’, seizing total 18.64 kg crude heroin in back-to-back operations near Lucknow (U.P.). Three key members of an inter-state trafficking network have been arrested. The contraband originated from North-Eastern State and were being trafficked for consumption in Uttar Pradesh.

Developing first precise inputs from the CBN MP Unit regarding drug movement from the North-East region to Lucknow, joint teams from CBN MP and UP units established a strategic cordon along the Sultanpur–Lucknow Highway on the intervening night of August 20–21, 2026.

Following continuous tracking from at different Toll Plazas, the strike team intercepted an Assam-registered Hyundai Creta at near Lucknow on August 21. The vehicle was found empty and the occupants claimed innocence. Operational officers grew suspicious when the vehicle’s occupants on questioning disclosed to have refueled four times within a span of just 500 km. A physical tapping test of the fuel tank confirmed a hollow acoustic anomaly. At the CBN Office in Lucknow, technical assistance was utilized to dismantle the fuel tank, exposing a specially fabricated compartment holding 25 waterproof packages containing 16.46 kg of crude heroin. Both suspects were arrested.

In another (second) actionable intelligence developed by the CBN UP Unit indicated a heavy truck transporting contraband along the Siliguri–Lucknow corridor. CBN teams tracked the vehicle across multiple toll plazas before intercepting it near Barabanki. A systematic physical search revealed 2.16 kg crude heroin concealed inside a specially constructed secret chamber within the vehicle’s body frame. One suspect was arrested.


All three suspects have been booked under stringent provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. Both transport vehicles and the entire contraband consignment have been confiscated. Comprehensive follow-up financial and logistical investigations are currently underway to trace upstream suppliers in the North-East and dismantle connected downstream distribution channels.

 

Key seizures at a glance

  • Total Seized Drugs: 18.64 kg (16.48 kg from a Car and 2.16 kg from a heavy commercial vehicle)
  • Vehicles Impounded: one Assam-registered Hyundai Creta, one Heavy Commercial Truck.
  • Total Arrests: 3 Suspects (arrested under the NDPS Act, 1985)
  • Concealment Methods: Fabricated fuel tank cavity and secret body chambers in Truck.

****

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the values of compassion and contentment
Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 8:08AM by PIB Delhi


The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, said that compassion brings self-respect and contentment brings true happiness. He noted that this spirit further strengthens the bonds of cooperation and harmony in society.

The Prime Minister shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam-

“कारुण्येनात्मनो मानं तृष्णां च परितोषतः।

उत्थानेन जयेत्तन्द्रीं वितर्कं निश्चयाज्जयेत्॥”

The Subhashitam conveys that self-respect is achieved by showing kindness or compassion to others. Greed is overcome by being satisfied at one's fortune in life. One must conquer laziness, dubious reasoning and indecisiveness by exertion and entrepreneurship.

The Prime Minister wrote on X;

“करुणा से आत्म-सम्मान और संतोष से सच्ची खुशी मिलती है। इसी भाव से समाज में सहयोग और सद्भाव की डोर और सशक्त होती है।

कारुण्येनात्मनो मानं तृष्णां च परितोषतः।

उत्थानेन जयेत्तन्द्रीं वितर्कं निश्चयाज्जयेत्॥”

The programme was organised as part of the Zoo’s ongoing Citizen Science Initiative, which aims to encourage public participation in biodiversity…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Zoological Park organises 2nd ‘Tree Walk’ and 11th ‘Sunday Bird Walk’ at Delhi Zoo
42 Bird Species and 40 Tree Species documented during the Nature Walks at NZP
Posted On: 23 AUG 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

The National Zoological Park, New Delhi successfully organised the 2nd edition of ‘Tree Walk @ NZP’ along with its 11th Sunday Bird Walk on 23rd August 2026. The programme was organised as part of the Zoo’s ongoing Citizen Science Initiative, which aims to encourage public participation in biodiversity documentation, monitoring and conservation awareness.

The Tree Walk was conducted from 7:00 AM to 10:00 AM under the expert guidance of Dr. C. R. Magesh (Scientist-D), while the Bird Walk was conducted under the guidance of ornithology expert Dr. Paritosh  Ahmed. The programme received an enthusiastic response from nature enthusiasts, students, wildlife photographers, biodiversity researchers, NZP interns and volunteers, as well as citizens interested in nature and conservation. A total of 25 participants took part in the walks. The programme was attended by the Director of National Zoological Park, zoo officials, interns, volunteers and resource experts, who guided and supported the participants throughout the activities.

 

During the walks, participants documented 42 bird species, with observations of more than 300 individual birds, along with 40 tree species in the walk area. A notable highlight of the Bird Walk was the presence of more than 150 Painted Storks, which arrived at the National Zoological Park during the second week of August and have begun nesting on trees in and around the pond. Their arrival and nesting are encouraging indicators of the ecological value of the Zoo’s wetland and tree habitats. The nesting activity also provides an important opportunity for visitors, interns, volunteers and citizen scientists to observe and understand natural bird behaviour and breeding ecology.

During the programme, Dr. Paritosh shared an interesting account of a male Painted Stork named ‘Ringo’, which has been observed making its nest in the same area for the past four years. Further observations and study of the bird are being continued by zoo interns. The Tree Walk provided participants with practical guidance on tree identification using features such as leaf morphology, bark characteristics, flowers, fruits and canopy structure. Participants also gained insights into the valuable ecosystem services provided by trees, including carbon sequestration, air purification, temperature regulation, soil conservation and the creation of habitats for diverse flora and fauna.

The programme encouraged participants to systematically document their observations while developing a deeper appreciation of the critical role of trees in sustaining healthy urban ecosystems. It also provided an opportunity to explore and document the diversity of trees and birds within the Zoo landscape while learning scientific methods of observation, species identification and biodiversity data recording.

Speaking on the occasion, the Director, National Zoological Park, emphasised that trees form the foundation of healthy ecosystems by supporting countless species and providing invaluable ecosystem services. He noted that Nature Walks @ NZP strengthen public awareness, encourage citizen participation in biodiversity documentation and inspire greater responsibility towards conserving urban forests and green landscapes.

The event concluded with an interactive discussion and feedback session, followed by a group photograph of the participants, experts and zoo officials. Participation in each Sunday Nature Walk is limited to 20–25 participants to ensure a meaningful and quality learning experience. 

Prior registration is mandatory and is accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Interested participants may register through the designated Google Form, which remains open from Monday to Friday each week. The registration link is available on the official website of the National Zoological Park, New Delhi, and through the ‘NZP Sathi’ mobile application.

The next nature walks — ‘Sunday Reptile, Amphibians and Mollusc Walk’ and ‘Sunday Bird Walk’ — are scheduled to be held on 30th August, 2026 (Sunday).

 

*****

VM/SK
